syn_startup_news.notes: News article about Kontora (vendor null, blog). Currency EUR from the euro sign. The plan range '€19 to €99 per month' gives two entries (from / up_to) with no plan names, product Kontora. Kasse is an add-on at €10 a month; which plans take it is not stated (plan null). The older tariff's €15 has no period stated; it is the price legacy customers pay (subscription, period null). The enterprise tier is 'priced individually' (quote). Werkly's €29 per user per month is a specific competitor price stated as fact: labelled as a price of the product Werkly. The 'average competing tool ... around €35' is a competitor average, not a price. Funding, revenue, market size, growth %, counts, years and rating are not prices.

syn_payments_uk.notes: UK payments pricing, GBP throughout; pence converted (20p = 0.20). Card rates are per transaction, one entry per amount (percentage and fixed part separately), plan from the card heading, card type kept in notes only (UK cards / Non-UK cards). The announcement's 0% fees on the first £1,000 is an introductory transaction rate (promotional); £1,000 is the volume threshold. Plus is £19/month excl. VAT, billed monthly per the FAQ. The £99 setup fee is the normal fee (the waiver before 31 March 2027 is a promotion on it, the amount itself is not promotional). 'Processing over £500,000 a year' is a volume threshold for Custom, which is a quote. Other fees have no plan (attribution clear to the named fee). Instant payouts 1% with a 50p minimum: minimum labelled as pricing_type minimum. The FAQ worked example (£1.60 in fees on a £100 payment, £98.40 paid out) is a calculation from the rates above, not a price point: not prices.

syn_grocery_in.notes: Indian grocery listing, INR. 'MRP inclusive of all taxes' is a page-level note; tile prices are labelled tax included. Each tile: offer price (pricing_type unit, product = tile name, the pack size is part of the name), struck-through MRP (labelled as a price: it is the stated maximum retail price, the regular price; the offer below it on a tile with a % OFF badge is promotional), and the per-unit price in brackets (basis kg / piece). Coriander is priced per bunch. Delivery charge ₹29 below ₹499 labelled as a per-order fee (transaction). ₹499 thresholds, ₹50 off, % OFF badges, cashback 5% and its ₹100 cap, counts and pin code are not prices. The head JSON-LD ItemList repeats the offer prices of rice, dal and mango (layout json_ld); promotional and tax copied from the visible tiles they describe.

syn_mobile_au.notes: Australian mobile plans; the page states 'All prices are in AUD and include GST', so currency AUD (not assumed) and tax included everywhere. Card data allowances are recorded as included. Medium's $30/mth is the limited-time price for the first 6 months (promotional), $40/mth the price after. syn_crm_compare.notes: Comparison article (vendor null); product = tool. 'Prices as of March 2026' sets effective for the whole page. Bare $ with no other dollar: USD assumed; Dealbloom's table price is in EUR excl. VAT. Table column 'Paid plans from' gives bound from. Pipewise: $15/user/mo billed annually and $18 month-to-month (same starting tier, per user read from the row; bound from). Pipewise's free plan is $0 for up to 2 users. Huddle CRM is contact sales (quote). Pipewise Growth $39/user/month; its AI assistant is 'an extra $10' with no period stated (add_on, period null). Clientory's $299 onboarding fee is setup. The Dealbloom anecdote ('paid $29 a month during the trial period, ... unclear whether that included any add-ons') does not establish which plan or what the amount covered: attribution ambiguous; whether it is an introductory/trial price is unjudgeable. The $35 average is a competitor average. $1M revenue and counts are not prices.
